Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through FinTrust’s use case and constraints. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps focused on the access-control/privacy items you asked about: 

Summary of today's ask (from FinTrust):
- Confirmation on RBAC roles and least-privilege defaults for production data.
- Details on support access / break-glass procedures (how we grant temporary elevated access and audit it).
- Data retention & residency options for PII and logs.
- Sample security artefacts you can share with procurement.

What I can send now (attached):
- Redwood_Security_Snapshot_SOC2.pdf — short SOC 2 overview and controls map.
- access-controls-diagram.png — high-level RBAC model and break-glass flow.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll follow up with the detailed answers below and attach a short ’support access playbook’.
2) Monica (cc) will run a 30-minute technical follow-up next week to walk through RBAC roles and the break-glass demo. Are mornings PST on Tue/Wed possible?
3) If helpful, we can provide a redlined sample data-processing clause and a short runbook for audit evidence.

Quick answers (high level):
- RBAC: Role templates (admin, engineer, readonly, support) + custom roles. Least-privilege enforced by default; engineers need explicit grant for production tokens.
- Support access: Temporary sessions issued via audited jump protocol; approvals logged and e-mail-notified to customer admins.
- Retention: Configurable retention buckets per-stream (30/90/365/retain-until-delete) with optional auto-purge for PII.
- Residency: Hosted regions in us-west, us-east, eu-west; dedicated/private deployments available for strict residency.

Attachments: I’ve attached the two items above — will follow with the playbook and a sample clause.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Hi Sofia —

Thanks — see answers below and the additional attachments (support-access-playbook.pdf). I’ve also added Dev to this thread so he can prep a short demo of the break-glass flow during next week’s call.

Answers (detailed):
1) Break-glass approval flow:
   - Primary approver: FinTrust admin(s) (we integrate with your SSO/SCIM and honor the customer admin group).
   - Support trigger: Redwood support/session request is opened; an approval request is sent to the customer admin(s) via e-mail and Slack (if integrated).
   - Fallback: If no response within the SLA window, an emergency break-glass can be routed to a designated security approver at FinTrust and logged as an exception.
   - All break-glass events are time-limited (15/60/180 min) and auto-revoked.

2) Audit logs & SIEM integration:
   - Logged fields: timestamp, internal_user_id, external_user_identity (SSO), approver_id, justification_text, session_start/stop, privileged_commands_executed (hashed), IP, region, request_id.
   - Export: Logs export via secure syslog or S3 export; we provide a CloudWatch/Datadog integration as well.

3) RBAC & SSO:
   - Yes: roles can be mapped to Okta groups via SCIM. You can also create custom roles in-console; default least-privilege templates provided.

4) Data retention & subject requests:
   - Retention: configurable retention policies per dataset/route.
   - Object-level purge: supported for customer-owned data; we provide an API and portal workflow for DSARs (subject access/deletion). Purges are logged and irreversible.

Attachments included: 
- Redwood_Security_Snapshot_SOC2.pdf — SOC 2 summary.
- access-controls-diagram.png — RBAC + break-glass flow.
- support-access-playbook.pdf — steps for initiating/approving support access, sample approval emails, and audit evidence checklist.

Sample DPA clause (high level excerpt):
"Redwood agrees to process Personal Data only in accordance with Customer's documented instructions. Redwood shall implement and maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards appropriate to the risk, including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and audit logging. Subprocessor access to Customer Data will be governed by contract and limited to support tasks necessary to provide the Service."

Next steps:
- Dev: can you schedule a 30-minute technical demo (break-glass + RBAC mapping) for Tue 10 Aug between 9–11am PST?
- Sofia: if that window works, we’ll send a calendar invite and a short deck.

Let me know if you need anything else for procurement.

Best,
Marissa
